episodes.189209: A building was damaged from a late afternoon lightning strike.
episodes.189222: Considerable atmospheric instability and deep-layer shear produced severe thunderstorms  in the late afternoon along a cold frontal boundary that was stretched across the NE Midlands of SC.
episodes.189274: Severe thunderstorms developed along and ahead of a cold front when then ran into the sea breeze. The environment was quite unstable and the shear was fairly strong.
episodes.189275: Severe thunderstorms developed along and ahead of a cold front when then ran into the sea breeze. The environment was quite unstable and the shear was fairly strong.
episodes.189788: A cold front draped across central North Carolina served as a focus for thunderstorm redevelopment during the afternoon as the cold front shifted slowly south. Supercells developed across the southern Piedmont, Sandhills, and southern Coastal Plain Counties. The severe storms went on to produce prolific hail ranging from ping pong to just over hen egg size across southern portions of central North Carolina. One supercell thunderstorm went on to produce 3-4 inch hail in nearby Robeson County.
episodes.190115: A stalled front sagging southward was able to provide enough lift to begin convection along a narrow band in Central GA. Thunderstorms had a brief period to become strong to marginally severe where MUCAPE was sufficient and shear was modest at best. A couple thunderstorms did result in damaging winds across the area.
episodes.190612: A strong trough over northeastern Mexico pushed a cold front down into South Texas late in the evening of the 20th into the early morning hours of the 21st, setting up a favorable environment for supercells. A few supercells developed over the Brush Country and Victoria Crossroads. Large hail was reported in Goliad and Duval Counties.
episodes.190856: An upper level disturbance and a cold front produced one round of thunderstorms the evening of Thursday April 18, a few of which contained large hail. The front eventually stalled, setting the stage for a second round of thunderstorms (this time elevated above the frontal layer) on the night of the 19th and continuing into the 20th. A few storms produce marginally severe hail, and heavy rain generated flooding in a few locations in North Texas.
episodes.190931: A shortwave trough ejecting out into the southern Great Plains aided in the development of a convective system across the Permian Basin. This convective system resulted in flooding across portions of the Permian Basin.
episodes.190978: Isolated thunderstorms developed near the North Carolina/South Carolina border during the afternoon. One of the storms produced hail and gusty winds in Gaston County.
episodes.190981: An isolated thunderstorm developed over the North Carolina foothills during the afternoon and steadily intensified as it moved southeast into the South Carolina Piedmont. The storm evolved into an intense supercell over York County and produced downburst winds up to 90 mph and very large hail up to baseball size. Wind-driven hail caused extensive structural damage in the city of Rock Hill.
episodes.191126: A cold front shifted slowly south across Central and East Texas on the morning of April 20th, aided by widespread showers and thunderstorms from Southwest Texas through North Central and into Northeast Texas. Warm and moist southerly low-level flow had persisted throughout the morning, and this resulted in increased low-level convergence along the frontal zone while also destabilizing the downstream air mass. Pre-frontal dewpoints ranged from the upper 60s to the lower 70s. Additionally, filtered heating allowed temperatures to rise into the lower 80s. These low-level thermodynamic conditions resulted in air mass destabilization while any convective inhibition eroded, leading to the warm and moist conditions with moderate buoyancy of near 1500 J/kg. Given these parameters, an isolated strong thunderstorm managed to produce nickel size hail near Gilmer in Upshur County.
episodes.191285: A weak landspout was observed near Rusty Point, AK, by a member of the general public in Anchorage. A lenticular cloud was noted over the mountain peak at the time, which was attached to the landspout. With no radar available to aid in the landspout's diagnosis, it is theorized that downsloping winds, enhanced by south and southeasterly winds, created an area of wind shear in a topographically varying region, which was then lifted vertically with an upslope flow, thus producing the observed landspout.
episodes.191321: A severe thunderstorm occurred in Escambia County, Alabama that produced severe hail up to golf ball size.

NWS storm survey found a virtually continuous path of downburst damage from the city of York, southeast across the city of Rock Hill, across the Catawba community to the Lancaster County border. Widespread trees and power lines were blow down along this path. Numerous homes experienced mostly minor structural damage.
Ham radio operator reported 3/4 inch hail.

Multiple sources reported an almost continuous swath of very large hail ranging from 2-inch diameter up to baseball size from the city of York through the city of Rock Hill. Intense downbursts producing wind gusts as high as 90 mph resulted in areas of wind-driven hail that produced extensive damage to structures and vehicles. The largest hail and most intense damage was in the city of Rock Hill, especially just south of the city center. Extensive roof damage, blown out windows, and facade/siding damage shredded by very large hail resulted in more than a dozen structures being considered a total loss. Hundreds of other structures experienced at least minor damage. Thousands of vehicles were damaged or destroyed. A few minor injuries also occurred.

Within a larger swath of wind damage, an especially intense downburst producing wind gusts of around 90 mph developed over the city of Rock Hill. Mostly minor structural damage due solely to wind occurred to hundreds of structures, mainly just south of the city center.
